title: callgraph
summary: Prints an N-deep resolved call tree for a symbol, in either direction
intro: Read this when you want to know who calls a routine, or what it calls, several levels deep. callgraph prints an N-deep resolved call tree for a symbol in either direction, guarded against cycles. The IDE menu item always walks 3 levels; the CLI takes --depth.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint callgraph --qname <X> [--direction callers|callees] [--depth N] --db PATH [--json|--format text|json] (N-deep resolved call tree; cycle-guarded)
help: drag-lint callgraph --qname <X> [--direction callers|callees] [--depth N] --db PATH [--json|--format text|json]   (N-deep resolved call tree; cycle-guarded; another --format exits 2 -- dot/mermaid: reverse-calltree)

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Call Tree (callers or callees, N-deep)...
steps: Put the caret on the routine in the editor (the name box is prefilled from the caret)
Choose drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Call Tree (callers or callees, N-deep)...
Confirm the qualified name, then answer Yes for callers or No for callees; the depth is fixed at 3 in the IDE (use the CLI --depth for other depths) and the call tree opens as a report

questions.ask: Who calls this routine, several levels deep?
What does this routine call, several levels deep?
